## Code Review: `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/review_target.py`

### Critical (blocks merge)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 1 | review_target.py:11 | Security — SQL injection | OWASP Top 10 / coding-standards.md §3.2 (validate at boundaries) | `order_id` is interpolated directly into a SQL string via f-string. Any caller passing an unsanitized `order_id` (e.g. from a request) can inject arbitrary SQL. | Use a parameterized query: `db_conn.execute("SELECT total FROM orders WHERE id = ?", (order_id,))` (or the driver's placeholder syntax). |
| 2 | review_target.py:24 | Security — SQL injection (same defect, second occurrence) | OWASP Top 10 / coding-standards.md §3.2 | Same f-string interpolation pattern on the `UPDATE` statement. | Same fix — parameterize `order_id`. |
| 3 | review_target.py:19-22 | Anti-pattern — swallowed error | coding-standards.md §9 ("Catching/swallowing errors 'just in case' without a named failure mode") and §3.2 (handle errors at the appropriate layer) | A non-200 response from the payment gateway is silently converted to `return None`. The caller cannot distinguish "payment declined", "gateway timeout", and "no order found" — all collapse to `None`. In a payment path this risks orders being marked unpaid/paid inconsistently with no diagnostic trail. | Raise a typed exception (e.g. `PaymentFailedError(resp.status_code, resp.text)`) or return a `Result`/tagged union that carries the failure reason; let the caller (or an outer boundary) decide how to handle it. |

### Important (should fix before merge)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 4 | review_target.py:8-25 | SOLID — SRP violation | coding-standards.md §1.1 (one reason to change) | `process_order` reads from the DB, calls an external payment API, applies discount logic, and writes back to the DB — four responsibilities in one function. A change to the discount rule, the payment provider, or the persistence layer each forces an edit here. | Split into: a pure `apply_discount(total) -> float` (business logic, no I/O), a `PaymentGateway` port with a `charge(amount)` method, and an `OrderRepository` port with `get_total`/`mark_paid`. `process_order` becomes an orchestrator composing the three. |
| 5 | review_target.py:8-25 | Clean Architecture — DIP / layering | coding-standards.md §2.2, §5.1 | The function directly imports `requests` (infrastructure) and calls `db_conn.execute` with no abstraction — there is no port/interface between the (implicit) business logic and its infrastructure dependencies, so core logic cannot be tested or swapped without touching real I/O. | Define `PaymentGateway` and `OrderRepository` as protocols/interfaces owned by the core/business layer; inject concrete implementations (`StripeGateway`, `SqlOrderRepository`) from a composition root. |
| 6 | review_target.py:13 | Anti-pattern — magic number | coding-standards.md §3.1, §8 (no invented constants) | `500` (discount threshold) has no name and no `# source:` comment explaining why 500 was chosen. | Introduce a named, sourced constant, e.g. `BULK_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD = 500  # source: <business rule / ticket / doc>`. |
| 7 | review_target.py:14 | Anti-pattern — magic number | coding-standards.md §3.1, §8 (no invented constants) | `0.9` (10% discount multiplier) is an unnamed, unsourced constant. | Introduce a named, sourced constant, e.g. `BULK_DISCOUNT_MULTIPLIER = 0.9  # source: <business rule / ticket / doc>`. |

### Minor (optional, improve later)

| # | File:Line | Category | Principle | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----------|----------|-----------|-------|-----|
| 8 | review_target.py:8 | Reliability — missing type hints | coding-standards.md §3.2 (use the type system fully) | `order_id`, `db_conn` and the return value have no type annotations, so a `None` return (the swallowed-error path) is invisible in the signature. | Annotate: `def process_order(order_id: int, db_conn: Connection) -> float | None:` (or better, a typed `Result` once finding #3 is fixed). |

### Architecture assessment

This is a single free-standing function with no layer boundaries at all: business logic (discount calculation), a database adapter, and an HTTP payment adapter are fused together, violating the Dependency Rule (coding-standards.md §2.2) by construction — there's no core module that infrastructure could instead depend on. Beyond the two security-critical SQL-injection sites and the silently-swallowed payment failure, the structural fix (extracting a discount policy plus `PaymentGateway`/`OrderRepository` ports) would resolve the SRP and DIP findings together, since they share the same root cause: no separation between orchestration, business rules, and I/O.
